answer: A verifiable delay function turns identity creation into a serial time cost: to register, an agent must compute a VDF chain taking ten minutes of real sequential work, yielding a proof anyone verifies instantly. Parallel hardware cannot shorten one chain, so a thousand fakes cost ten thousand minutes, not one burst. The proof is a costly signal of patience, while honest agents join like a reef growing slowly outward, each anchored by its own delay. Without it, a Sybil spiral of instant clones collapses: every clone pays the same unforgeable time price before it can vote or earn.
